title: Past with {être} - Which Verbs, Which Endings
description: See which verbs build the past with {être}, and when the participle adds -e or -s.
can_do: Choose {avoir} or {être} for the past: {j'ai mangé}, {je suis allé}.
Make the participle agree after {être}: {elle est allée}, {ils sont allés}.
line: A small group of verbs and every reflexive verb build the past with {être}, and the participle then agrees with the subject.

parts.heading: {avoir} or {être}
text: Most verbs build the passé composé with {avoir}: {j'ai mangé}. A small group of verbs, most of them about coming and going, use {être}: {je suis allé}.
parts.note: Many {être} verbs come in opposite pairs: {aller} and {venir}, {arriver} and {partir}, {entrer} and {sortir}, {monter} and {descendre}.

parts.heading: Reflexive verbs take {être}
text: Every reflexive verb builds its past with {être}. The small pronoun stays in front of {être}: {je me suis levé}.

lines: Ce matin, je me suis réveillé.

parts.heading: The participle agrees
text: After {être}, the participle agrees with the subject, the way an adjective does. Add -e for a woman or a feminine noun, and -s for more than one. Reflexive verbs usually follow the same rule.
parts.note: A group of men and women takes the masculine: {Pierre et Marie sont allés}. After {avoir}, the participle does not agree with the subject: {elle a mangé}.

parts.heading: In a short story
text: Here are both rules together: {être} for coming and going, and an ending that matches the subject.

lines: Hier, Marie est arrivée à Paris.
Ce matin, elle s'est levée et elle est partie.
This morning she got up and she left.

checks.ask: Which verb builds its passé composé with {être}?
checks.why: {arriver} is a verb of coming and going: {je suis arrivé}. {manger} and {regarder} take {avoir}.

checks.ask: Which one means “She went to the café”?
checks.why: {aller} takes {être}, and the participle adds -e for {elle}: {elle est allée}.
{se préparer} is reflexive, so its past takes {être}, and the participle adds -s for {nous}.
